name: Thanh Ha Pottery Village
kicker: Pottery village west of the old town
summary: The pottery village in khối Nam Diêu, Thanh Hà ward. The craft index puts it 3 kilometres west-southwest of the old town. A heritage article says about 3 kilometres west, on the Thu Bồn, and dates the trade to more than 500 years, with the tiles on the old houses among its work. The fee, the hours, and the ride minutes are check on arrival.

body: The craft index places Thanh Hà in khối Nam Diêu, phường Thanh Hà, 3 kilometres west-southwest of the ancient town. A heritage article says the village is on the Thu Bồn bank, about 3 kilometres to the west, and that it was then in Cẩm Hà. Keep both bearings. The article gives the village more than 500 years and a busy stretch in the 16th and 17th centuries, when its pots and tiles were traded through the port. It also says Thanh Hà made the yin-yang roof tiles on the old houses.

The visit is the wheel and the yards that still use the old technique. The article describes a terracotta park of more than 6,500 square metres, with two buildings it compares to kilns, as a place that keeps the village’s pots. A May 2018 heritage note recognised both the village and that park as local tourism sites. The article’s story that workers came from Nghệ An and Thanh Hóa is told as tradition, so treat it as the village’s account.

No fee and no door hours are printed. The minutes from the old town are not printed either. All three are check on arrival. Go in the morning, and do not confuse this yard with the Museum of Trade Ceramics on Trần Phú. That museum is the old trade ware. This is the village that still throws pots.
